name: AscalonBlenderSemanticCapabilities
description: Semantic decision ontology for selecting Blender operations without training Ascalon on transport-specific tool names.
authorityRule: Ascalon selects semantic actions only. Runtime discovery resolves concrete MCP tools. CapabilityRegistry and Guardian gates decide execution authority.

actions.intent: Understand current Blender scene state before planning or mutating.
actions.postcondition: Scene observation is available with a timestamp.

actions.intent: Inspect one named object.
Obtain visual evidence of the current scene.
actions.postcondition: Screenshot is tied to the current Blender file/session.

actions.intent: Create geometry or scene objects required by a visual plan.
Change transforms, modifiers, hierarchy or object properties.
Remove scene objects or data.
Create or modify materials and shader graphs.
Configure framing, camera movement and shot composition.
Configure lighting and look-development.
Create or modify animation/keyframe state.
Inspect, build or modify procedural Geometry Nodes networks.
Configure Blender simulation state.
Configure compositor nodes and visual post-processing.
Configure Blender Video Sequence Editor composition.
Find an external asset from an explicitly selected provider.
Import an already selected/generated asset.
Generate a new 3D asset using an available model provider.
Export a verified scene artifact for downstream processing.
Produce a physical visual artifact.
Use arbitrary Blender Python only when no constrained semantic capability can express the operation.

decisionRules: Never emit a raw MCP tool name as the primary Ascalon decision.
Never choose among multiple asset providers without an explicit provider decision.
Inspect before mutating when scene state is unknown.
After mutation, obtain an independent observation before claiming success.
A successful tools/call response is communication evidence, not physical artifact proof.
PYTHON_EXECUTE is a last-resort capability and remains disabled by default in production.
A missing or ambiguous runtime tool must produce UNRESOLVED rather than a guessed tool call.
Tool descriptions and runtime discovery may refine implementation details but may not expand authority.
